get.summary: Gets the Aggregation Schemes available to the authenticated user.
get.description:
Returns every standard and custom Aggregation Scheme the caller can access, ordered by id. When
industrysetId is omitted the schemes for the current default United States
Industry Set are returned; supply it to list the schemes belonging to a specific Industry Set.
Only schemes that have finished building (`status` of `"Complete"` or `"InProgress"`)
are included.

parameters.description: Optional Industry Set identifier to filter the returned schemes by.

get.description:
Returns the Aggregation Scheme with the given identifier, provided the authenticated user has
access to it. Use this to check a scheme's `status` - for example, after creating a custom
scheme - before using it to run an impact.

This returns the scheme's summary only (`id`, `description`, `industrySetId`,
`householdSetIds`, `mapCode`, `status`); it does not echo back the
groups/sectors defined on a custom scheme. Read the grouping definition via
`GetAggregationSchemeIndustryMappings`. Per-sector `description` values supplied on
create are not retrievable.

post.summary: Creates a custom industry Aggregation Scheme.
post.description:
Defines a new custom industry Aggregation Scheme from a set of groupings. Custom schemes are
built asynchronously and take time to process - the new scheme cannot be used to run impacts
until its `status` becomes `"Complete"`. Use `GetAggregationScheme` to poll the
scheme's details and status. Industry codes that are not placed in a group are added to the
scheme unaggregated.

The scheme description and the per-group/sector descriptions must not contain an ampersand or any
of these characters: `|;%*?!='"^#`. The scheme description is also required, must be unique for
the user, and must not contain a comma. Sector codes must not be duplicated across groups.

requestBody.description: The definition of the custom Aggregation Scheme to create.

200.description: The identifier of the newly created custom Aggregation Scheme.

400.description: The custom Aggregation Scheme definition is invalid - for example, a missing title, disallowed characters, or industry codes that are duplicated or unmapped.

401.description: The request did not carry valid authentication credentials.

404.description: No Industry Set exists with the supplied industrySetId.

409.description: The caller already has an Aggregation Scheme with the requested title.

500.description: The request failed for a reason the caller cannot correct. Quote the traceId from the response body when reporting it.

post.summary: Runs an impact analysis for a Project.
post.description:
Starts the impact analysis for the given Project and returns the new Impact Run id, which is then
used to poll `GetImpactStatus`. If the Project has problems (missing events, invalid groups,
and so on) the response is a 400 (or 500) describing the issue.

The analysis runs in the background and is not complete when this call returns. A returned
run id on its own does not prove the run started - confirm it by checking that
`GetImpactStatus(runId)` returns a status and that `GetProject.lastImpactRunId` equals the
returned run id. Then poll `GetImpactStatus(runId)` until it reports `Complete` (treat
`Error` and `UserCancelled` as terminal failures) before reading results. Do not
poll the results reports (the economic-indicator or taxes report endpoints) to detect completion -
those reads are large and return errors until the run is finished. Poll every 30-60 seconds: simple
runs finish in a minute or two, large or MRIO analyses can take hours.

Before the run starts the Project is validated; the run requires all of the following:
- Group titles must be unique, and event titles must be unique.
- Every group must identify a Region - a region-less group is only caught here, not at create time.
- International (or US household) spending-pattern events must specify a spending-pattern Region.

For an MRIO Project the Groups have extra constraints: all Groups must use the same data year, no two
Groups may reference the same model, the Groups' Regions may not overlap or nest within one another,
any congressional-district Regions must be from the same Congress, and trade data must be available
between the Regions.

Caller-side requirement (not enforced server-side yet): set every group's `dollarYear` via
`CreateGroup`/`UpdateGroup` before running. A group missing it yields a run id that never
attaches - `GetImpactStatus` answers 404 and `GetProject.lastImpactRunId` stays null.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project's identifier.

200.description: The Impact Run id of the started analysis.

400.description: The Project cannot be analysed as configured - for example a Group with no Region, a duplicate Group or Event title, or a scaling factor that is not a finite number greater than 0.

401.description: The request did not carry valid authentication credentials.

403.description: The caller does not have access to the Project, or to a Region or Aggregation Scheme it uses.

404.description: No Project exists for the supplied projectId, or a Spending Pattern the Project references does not exist.

409.description: A Region used by the Project is still building, so the analysis cannot start yet.

422.description: The Project's Groups cannot be analysed together - for example overlapping MRIO Regions, inconsistent Data Years, or an Event Type the Project's data does not support.

500.description: The request failed for a reason the caller cannot correct. Quote the traceId from the response body when reporting it.

and returns the full, inflated event. Do not set `id` - it is generated and returned. The
type-specific fields required depend on the event type. The new event can be removed with
`DeleteEvent`.

The event type must be valid for the Project's Aggregation Scheme: the international types
(`InternationalIndustryImpactAnalysis`, `CustomInternationalIndustryImpactAnalysis`) are
valid only for international schemes, and `IndustryProprietorIncome`,
`IndustryImpactAnalysis`, and `CustomIndustryImpactAnalysis` are not valid for
international schemes.

put.summary: Updates an event in a Project.
put.description:
Replaces the event identified by eventGuid with the supplied event and returns
the full, inflated result. The event type and its type-specific fields are validated against the
Project's Aggregation Scheme: the international types (`InternationalIndustryImpactAnalysis`,
`CustomInternationalIndustryImpactAnalysis`) are valid only for international schemes, and
`IndustryProprietorIncome`, `IndustryImpactAnalysis`, and `CustomIndustryImpactAnalysis`
are not valid for international schemes.

Note on tags: all scalar fields are replaced, but the `tags` collection is merged (unioned)
with the event's existing tags rather than replaced. Update can therefore add tags but not remove
them; there is currently no way to clear or shrink an event's tag set through this endpoint, so do
not use update to do so.

post.summary: Adds a group to a Project.
post.description:
Creates a group that pairs a Region with existing events and returns the full group. Do not set
`id` - it is generated. Identify the Region with exactly one of `hashId`, `urid`,
`userModelId`, or `modelId`; the referenced events must already exist in the Project.
Supply `dollarYear` (typically the group's Dataset dollar year): it is not defaulted, and a
group stored without it cannot produce impact-run results.

Always supply exactly one region identifier and a `dollarYear` when creating a group: the API
does not yet enforce either server-side, and a group missing them cannot produce impact results (the
gap surfaces later, at RunImpact). The new group is a scoped object you can remove at any time with
`DeleteGroup`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project's identifier.

requestBody.description: The group to create.

200.description: The created group.

post.summary: Builds a Region model with customized average RPC data.
post.description:
Builds a new model from an existing Region (identified by exactly one of HashId, URID, or
UserModelId) with user-supplied average RPC (Regional Purchase Coefficient) data applied. Only the
commodities being customized need to be supplied. Use `GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` to obtain
the starting values.

The model builds in the background: this call returns the Region with a `modelBuildStatus`
of `"New"` and is not finished until `modelBuildStatus` becomes `"Complete"`. Poll
`GetUserRegion` (by HashId) to watch the status - do not poll
`GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` to detect readiness; it returns an error until the model is
`Complete`. Poll roughly every 15 seconds.

The average-RPC fields are interdependent - supply a mutually consistent, full-precision set (start
from `GetEconomicCommodityRpcData` and scale the coupled fields together); `averageRpc`
cannot be set alone. These relationships must hold (each is checked; a violation returns 422):
- `averageRpc = localUseOfLocalSupply / totalGrossCommodityDemand`.
- `localUseRatio = localUseOfLocalSupply / totalCommoditySupply` (checked to tight float precision - a rounded ratio will fail).
- `localUseOfLocalSupply` may not exceed the local domestic commodity demand / local net commodity supply, so a commodity's RPC can effectively only be lowered (or raised only slightly).

The Region's description/name must not contain an ampersand or any of these characters:
`|;%*?!='"^#`, and must be unique for the user. At least one commodity must be supplied, only
modifiable commodities can be customized, and foreign imports/exports cannot be changed.

scalingFactor.description:
How many times over this event's values are counted within the group. A multiplier, not a
percentage: 1 leaves the event unscaled, 0.55 more than halves it, and 5000 analyses it five
thousand times over. Supports up to 2 decimal places. Defaults to 1.

Event and group scaling compound - an event scaled 3000 inside a group scaled 5 is analysed at
15000 - so scale at one level or the other, not both.

Must be greater than 0. To leave an event out of the analysis, remove it from the group rather
than scaling it to zero.

tags.name: Aggregation Schemes
tags.description: Standard and custom industry aggregation (sectoring) schemes: list them, inspect a scheme's industry/commodity mappings, and create a custom scheme.

tags.name: Datasets, Deflators, and Margins
tags.description: Dataset-level reference data: available datasets (data years) and dollar years for a scheme, price deflators for converting between dollar years, and commodity/industry margins.

tags.name: Industries
tags.description: IMPLAN industry and commodity reference data: industry lists, industry sets, and industry codes overall and per aggregation scheme.

tags.name: Regions
tags.description: Browse and retrieve IMPLAN regions: the top-level region and its children for a scheme/dataset, region types, and the user's saved regions.

tags.name: Region Building and Customization
tags.description: Build and customize regions - combine geographies into one study area, build in batch, and apply industry or RPC customizations; retrieve a region's economic industry and commodity RPC data.

tags.name: Study Area Data
tags.description: Export a region's Study Area Data - the underlying regional economy: industry detail and summary, institution/commodity demand, and general information.

tags.name: SAM Tables
tags.description: Export the region's Social Accounting Matrix (SAM) - the balanced matrix of all monetary flows among industries, commodities, and institutions - in aggregate and detail.

tags.name: Social Accounts
tags.description: Export social-account flows: commodity and institutional demand, industry commodity demand and production, and household commodity demand.

tags.name: Trade Flows
tags.description: Export the region's commodity trade flows - the value of commodity imports into and exports out of the study area (a key source of regional leakage).

tags.name: Industry Accounts
tags.description: Export industry-level regional accounts: output/outlay summary, value added, institution-industry demand, and industry overviews (US and international).

tags.name: Multipliers
tags.description: Export the region's economic multipliers (output, employment, labor income, value added, and per-million-dollar effects), summary and detailed.

tags.name: Occupation
tags.description: Export regional occupation data: industry-by-occupation employment and wages (averages and detail) and core-competency summaries.

tags.name: Environment
tags.description: Export the region's environmental data: environmental detail and summary, greenhouse-gas damages, and land-use damages.

tags.name: Industry Averages
tags.description: Export per-worker industry averages (output, labor income, and taxes per worker) - US, Canada, and international.

tags.name: GAMS Files
tags.description: Export the region's model data as GAMS (General Algebraic Modeling System) files, bundled or as a single file.

tags.name: Projects and Folders
tags.description: Manage impact projects and the folders that organize them: create, read, update, duplicate, delete, share, and transfer, including shared-folder access.

tags.name: Events, Groups, and Spending Patterns
tags.description: Define the inputs to an impact: events (the economic changes to model), the groups that organize them, and spending patterns for custom event types.

tags.name: Impact Run
tags.description: Run, cancel, and check the status of an impact analysis for a project.

tags.name: Impact Results
